question: Which insect spreads the malaria parasite to humans?

options.A: Housefly
options.B: Female Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Tsetse fly
options.D: Male Culex mosquito

question: A patient with Pick's disease tries to eat paper wrappers and craves tons of sugar. How should you understand this?

options.A: It indicates the patient is suffering from severe iron-deficiency anemia.
options.B: It is a typical oral and dietary manifestation caused by temporal lobe damage.
options.C: It is a deliberate attempt by the patient to seek attention from staff.
options.D: It proves the patient has developed a secondary bacterial throat infection.

explanation: When the temporal lobe is affected, patients often develop strange eating habits, like craving sweets or trying to swallow non-food items. It's not for attention—it's the disease at work! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the main goal of gathering public health surveillance data?

options.A: To guide health policy and practical actions
options.B: To increase the cost of medical treatments
options.C: To punish clinics that report too many sick patients
options.D: To fill up hospital filing cabinets with paperwork

explanation: We don't collect health data just to sit on shelves! It's meant to be put to work for planning and stopping diseases in our communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h2)

question: Why must disaster planning focus heavily on local government areas?

options.A: National laws forbid federal agencies from entering disaster zones
options.B: Local councils have more advanced medical equipment than federal hospitals
options.C: Disasters happen locally and require immediate community-level action
options.D: Local governments are the only bodies allowed to receive foreign aid

explanation: You got it! Because emergencies hit specific communities directly, local prep ensures rescue and relief kick off instantly without waiting for outside help. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h1)

question: What does an operating budget typically cover for a nursing unit?

options.A: The purchase of brand new hospital buildings and elevators
options.B: Emergency funds kept strictly for natural disasters
options.C: Long-term investments in overseas stock markets
options.D: Day-to-day expenses like staff salaries and routine medical supplies

explanation: Think of the operating budget as the money that pays for everyday running costs, like paying staff and buying routine ward supplies. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h4)

question: What do we mean by the 'window of implantation' in human reproduction?

options.A: The brief number of days when the uterine lining is receptive to a blastocyst
options.B: The days when the cervix opens to allow sperm to enter the uterus
options.C: The time period when the corpus luteum stops producing estrogen entirely
options.D: The exact hour when the sperm successfully penetrates the secondary oocyte

explanation: Correct! The womb is only ready to accept a tiny blastocyst during a very short, specific span of days each month. Learning this makes clinical practice much easier! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h3)

question: Which agency coordinates primary healthcare development at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)

explanation: The NPHCDA is the main federal body guiding PHC implementation all across Nigeria. Good to know for Nigerian nursing practice! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: Poor mouth care in vulnerable patients is closely linked to which serious lung problem?

options.A: Aspiration pneumonia
options.B: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Obstructive sleep apnea

explanation: Spot on! Germs hiding in a dirty mouth can slip down into the lungs and cause a nasty infection called aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h4)

question: What are you comparing when you perform a 'gap analysis' in community health?

options.A: The age of children versus the age of their grandparents
options.B: Current health status against desired health standards
options.C: The salary of nurses versus doctors in the clinic
options.D: Total population size against total land area in kilometers

explanation: A gap analysis simply looks at the gap between where the community's health is right now and the healthy standard we want them to achieve. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is a chemical barrier part of our innate defense?

options.A: Cytotoxic T-cell activation
options.B: Keratin in the outer skin layer
options.C: Lysozyme in tears and saliva
options.D: Antibodies produced by plasma cells

explanation: You're right! Lysozyme is a natural germ-killer found in our tears and saliva that breaks open bacterial walls. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of using the SBAR communication tool in the ward?

options.A: Punishing nurses who fail to document vital signs on time
options.B: Ensuring hospital administrators can track the exact location of staff
options.C: Replacing all written patient care charts with audio recordings
options.D: Providing a clear, standardized script to share critical patient data

explanation: SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) gives you a quick, reliable script so you can pass on vital patient info clearly and without panic. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h5)

question: What do we mean by 'second victim syndrome' in healthcare?

options.A: A secondary illness caught by a patient while staying in the ward
options.B: Emotional trauma experienced by a clinician after being involved in an error
options.C: The legal penalty given to a hospital following a malpractice lawsuit
options.D: The family member who has to pay extra hospital bills for an injury

explanation: Nurses and doctors who go through a tough adverse event often carry deep emotional pain. We call them the second victims. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T8#GNS312_U5_T8_h5)

question: What should you do right after pulling the needle out of a PPD injection site?

options.A: Pat the area gently with cotton without rubbing it
options.B: Massage the skin vigorously to help absorb the fluid
options.C: Apply a tight pressure bandage to stop any bleeding
options.D: Clean the skin again with a fresh alcohol swab

explanation: Hands off that bubble! Rubbing or massaging can push the fluid away or mess up the skin test results. Just a gentle dab if needed. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for patient selection before granting leave?

options.A: Presence of a supportive family or safe living arrangement
options.B: Having a large financial inheritance waiting outside
options.C: Demonstrated stability of acute psychiatric symptoms
options.D: Reliable cooperation with medication regimens

explanation: Money doesn't determine clinical readiness! Stability, safe housing, and taking medications are what truly matter for a successful leave. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which nursing action best demonstrates tertiary cancer prevention?

options.A: Encouraging a young adult to stop smoking cigarettes before any disease develops
options.B: Teaching arm exercises to a patient recovering from breast cancer surgery to prevent lymphedema
options.C: Providing educational pamphlets about the importance of getting a regular Pap smear
options.D: Administering a routine hepatitis B immunization to a healthcare worker

explanation: Managing complications and rehabilitating a patient post-treatment are core goals of tertiary prevention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h4)

question: What happens inside the small intestine of someone with celiac disease when they eat gluten?

options.A: Bacterial flora multiplies rapidly
options.B: Gastric acid production stops entirely
options.C: Excess mucus blocks digestion
options.D: Villi are damaged and flatten out

explanation: When gluten triggers an immune reaction in celiac disease, the tiny finger-like villi that absorb nutrients get flattened out. Great nursing insight to remember! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h2)

question: What is an epidemiological 'reservoir'?

options.A: The natural habitat where an infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The chemical disinfectant applied to counter harmful pathogens
options.C: The protective antibodies built up inside a patient's bloodstream
options.D: The medical equipment used to sterilize hospital surgical instruments

explanation: Think of a reservoir as home sweet home for the germ—where it hangs out, grows, and thrives over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h5)

question: How does keeping proper skeletal alignment help your joint health?

options.A: It eliminates the need for ligaments
options.B: It distributes physical weight evenly, preventing excessive wear
options.C: It increases the length of your leg bones
options.D: It stops synovial fluid from leaking out

explanation: Exactly! Good alignment shares body weight evenly across your joints so no single spot gets overworked and worn down too fast. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of health education in community nursing?

options.A: To empower individuals and groups to adopt healthy lifestyles
options.B: To diagnose complex medical disorders in hospital laboratories
options.C: To prescribe pharmaceutical drugs without a doctor's order
options.D: To generate revenue for local government health departments

explanation: Health education gives people the knowledge and skills they need to make healthy choices and prevent illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h6)

question: Which pattern of knowing represents the science of nursing derived from research?

options.A: Empirical knowing
options.B: Ethical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Personal knowing

explanation: Empirical knowing is your go-to science foundation—it relies on objective, observable data and actual research findings. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of these describes a democratic leadership style in healthcare?

options.A: Making all choices independently without consulting any staff members
options.B: Involving team members in discussions and valuing their input on decisions
options.C: Leaving the ward completely unattended to let nurses work on their own
options.D: Punishing staff members publicly for minor documentation errors

explanation: Democratic leaders bring the team together, listen to everyone's ideas, and make choices collaboratively. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h5)

question: Over which major chest muscle do the breasts primarily rest?

options.A: Intercostal muscle
options.B: Pectoralis major
options.C: Latissimus dorsi
options.D: Rectus abdominis

explanation: The pectoralis major muscle forms the muscular bed directly underneath the breast tissue on the anterior chest wall. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h1)

question: A child is rushed to the ward with severe, complicated malaria. What is the best first step regarding their medications?

options.A: Refuse treatment until the family pays cash for the full prescription
options.B: Wait for hospital accountants to review the family's bank statements
options.C: Send the parents out to buy drugs from a commercial chemist across the street
options.D: Provide necessary emergency anti-malarials immediately under the exemption policy

explanation: Spot on! Severe pediatric emergencies qualify for immediate medication access to save the child's life without delay. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the heart of reproductive rights?

options.A: The mandatory requirement for every adult to have children
options.B: Free cosmetic surgeries for all citizens reaching adulthood
options.C: Bodily autonomy and freedom from coercion in health decisions
options.D: Government control over family size and birth intervals

explanation: You nailed it! Reproductive rights mean every person has the right to make their own free choices about their body and family planning. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h6)

question: What control measure involves replacing a toxic chemical with a harmless water-based cleaner?

options.A: Engineering control
options.B: Administrative control
options.C: Elimination
options.D: Substitution

explanation: Think of 'substitution' like substituting a player on a football pitch—you take out the dangerous chemical and put in a safer one to do the same job! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h3)

question: Finding Escherichia coli (E. coli) in a water sample tells you what?

options.A: High concentrations of industrial heavy metals
options.B: Recent fecal contamination from humans or animals
options.C: Excessive mineral hardness from underground rocks
options.D: A normal and safe level of plant nutrients

explanation: Spot on! E. coli is our warning flag. Its presence proves that waste matter has found its way into the water supply. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h6)

question: You are caring for a patient with severe preeclampsia. Which symptom needs your immediate attention?

options.A: An oral temperature of thirty-seven degrees Celsius
options.B: A sudden report of a severe headache and blurred vision
options.C: A slight increase in anxiety about the hospital stay
options.D: A mild increase in appetite during the afternoon shift

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision in preeclampsia mean the brain is under pressure and a seizure might be near. Quick action saves lives here! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h5)

question: Where should a nurse properly document the details after an incident reportable mistake happens?

options.A: In the nursing notes section of the patient chart
options.B: In a private personal notebook kept at home
options.C: In the hospital's internal safety reporting system
options.D: On the front cover of the physical medical record

explanation: Incident reports go into special safety databases, separate from the patient chart, to help the hospital learn and track safety trends. [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h5)

question: How many hours of fasting are typically required before a standard GTT begins?

options.A: No fasting is needed
options.B: 18 to 24 hours
options.C: 8 to 14 hours
options.D: 2 to 4 hours

explanation: An overnight fast of 8 to 14 hours establishes an accurate baseline blood glucose level before the test beverage is consumed. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h3)

question: Which lab finding helps you spot Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) because it is usually missing in HHS?

options.A: Severe lack of fluid in the body
options.B: Presence of ketones and acidosis
options.C: Extremely high blood glucose levels
options.D: Altered level of consciousness

explanation: Great clinical thinking! DKA involves heavy fat breakdown that produces acidic ketones, whereas HHS spikes the sugar sky-high without major ketoacidosis. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h2)

question: In the emergency stabilization framework used before transport, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bandaging
options.B: Brain
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Breathing

explanation: Think of the trusty ABCDE framework! 'B' stands for Breathing, making sure air is moving properly into the lungs right after checking the airway. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which nutrient starts its chemical digestion in the oral cavity?

options.A: Triglycerides
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Salivary amylase is present in saliva and begins breaking down complex carbohydrates right inside the mouth. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why must patients with liver disease avoid taking casual painkillers like paracetamol without asking a doctor?

options.A: It neutralizes the effects of prescribed lactulose syrup
options.B: The liver has to process it, and it can cause more damage
options.C: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in liver patients
options.D: It increases the risk of dehydration and kidney failure

explanation: Medications like paracetamol are processed by the liver. When the liver is weak, these drugs can build up quickly and cause serious harm. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the medical term for a lack of oxygen to an unborn baby?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Foetal hyperglycemia
options.C: Intrauterine hypoxia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

explanation: Intrauterine hypoxia refers specifically to the state where a foetus experiences reduced oxygen levels in the womb. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h1)

question: Why should lab request forms never share the same pouch as a liquid specimen bottle?

options.A: To speed up the sorting process inside the central laboratory
options.B: To prevent the paperwork from being ruined if the specimen leaks
options.C: To comply with rules regarding medical record privacy
options.D: To ensure the laboratory technician reads the test name first

explanation: Great thinking! If a bottle leaks, it can soak and destroy the request form, making patient identification and testing impossible. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h4)

question: How does gender discrimination often show up inside everyday healthcare settings?

options.A: Via written notices refusing service to women
options.B: Through hidden biases in daily routines
options.C: By official hospital policy stating unequal care
options.D: Through mandatory fees for male patients

explanation: Institutional bias is usually subtle. It sneaks into everyday clinical routines and unspoken habits rather than being written down as an official rule. Great job thinking critically about this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h1)

question: How does trial leave differ mainly from occasional leave?

options.A: Trial leave is only given to patients who refuse oral medications
options.B: Trial leave lasts much longer, often weeks or months, acting as a test for discharge
options.C: Trial leave requires the patient to stay inside a locked community center
options.D: Trial leave completely severs the patient's connection to the hospital

explanation: Trial leave is an extended test run lasting weeks or months to see if the patient is truly ready to head home permanently. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why are art and creative therapies so helpful for trauma survivors?

options.A: They replace the need for professional psychiatric counseling
options.B: They completely cure post-traumatic stress disorder in one session
options.C: They allow expression of emotions that are hard to put into words
options.D: They force patients to relive painful memories out loud

explanation: Trauma can be really tough to talk about. Creative outlets like drawing or painting give patients a safe way to let those heavy feelings out. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is one of the most common ways cultural stigma affects people with mental health challenges?

options.A: Hospitals receive extra funding for psychiatric care
options.B: Individuals hide their symptoms and avoid seeking professional help
options.C: Families immediately bring patients to the clinic
options.D: Community members openly discuss their emotions

explanation: Stigma breeds fear and shame, making people suffer in silence rather than risk being judged by others. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h6)

question: How can a patient with severe upper body paralysis steer an automated wheelchair?

options.A: A heavy floor-based foot pedal
options.B: A sip-and-puff mechanism
options.C: A ceiling-mounted pull cord
options.D: A standard manual push rim

explanation: Brilliant! A sip-and-puff control lets patients steer simply by blowing into or inhaling through a small straw tube using breath pressure. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the most common opportunistic infection and leading cause of death in people with HIV?

options.A: Tetanus
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Cholera
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Tuberculosis (TB) is the top opportunistic infection we watch out for in patients with weakened immune systems. Catching it early saves lives! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h8)

question: How does a Root Cause Analysis differ from simply blaming an individual worker?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on financial losses rather than clinical outcomes
options.B: It investigates underlying systemic flaws rather than stopping at personal fault
options.C: It ensures that the guilty employee is fired immediately without appeal
options.D: It hides safety mistakes from hospital management and regulatory bodies

explanation: Root Cause Analysis asks 'Why did this happen?' instead of 'Who did this?'. It digs deep into workflow, equipment, and communication to fix the real problem. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is a common myth among young people regarding Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Regular screening helps catch hidden diseases
options.B: Condoms can help prevent transmission
options.C: People with STIs always look visibly sick
options.D: Some infections do not show early symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Many people are surprised to learn that numerous STIs show no early symptoms at all, meaning someone can feel completely healthy while carrying an infection. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h5)

question: What crucial details must always be included on a community health referral form?

options.A: The financial salary grade of the attending nurse
options.B: The personal home phone number of the village chief
options.C: Assessment findings and initial care given
options.D: A complete inventory of clinic furniture

explanation: You got it! The receiving hospital needs to know your assessment findings and what emergency treatments you already started before they arrived. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h6)

question: What is the very first step in the community health decision-making process?

options.A: Evaluate the final outcome
options.B: Allocate available funds
options.C: Develop alternative solutions
options.D: Identify the problem

explanation: You cannot solve an issue until you clearly define and recognize what the actual health problem is using data. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h3)

question: A nurse wants to refer a newly diagnosed, fearful patient to a support group. What is the best approach?

options.A: Leave a stack of group fliers on the waiting room table and say nothing
options.B: Discuss the patient's specific fears and explain what to expect at a meeting
options.C: Wait until the patient stops taking medications before mentioning any groups
options.D: Insist that attending the group is a legal requirement for getting medications

explanation: Effective referrals require personal guidance, addressing fears, and preparing the patient rather than just handing over a flier. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h5)

question: Why is MHPSS organized as a multi-layered pyramid instead of treating everyone the same way?

options.A: To ensure that the majority of people receive expensive medication first
options.B: To maximize the efficient use of limited resources while meeting varied community needs
options.C: To prove that psychological interventions are more important than basic food and water
options.D: To make sure specialized clinical staff handle every single case of mild stress

explanation: The pyramid helps us match the right level of help to how distressed someone is. That way, specialists aren't overwhelmed by mild stress, and everyone gets what they need! [learn more](GNS314_U6_T1#GNS314_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is measured during an anthropometric assessment?

options.A: Serum albumin levels
options.B: Daily water intake
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Blood pressure readings

explanation: Anthropometry involves physical body measurements like height, weight, and body mass index. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h3)

question: How do telehealth and remote monitoring help keep patients out of the hospital?

options.A: By eliminating all potential health risks associated with aging at home
options.B: By allowing nurses to catch early signs of clinical deterioration and intervene quickly
options.C: By stopping clients from taking prescribed medications incorrectly
options.D: By forcing clients to visit the outpatient clinic every single day

explanation: Catching small changes early means the care team can step in and fix things before a minor issue turns into an emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of using strict aseptic technique during invasive procedures?

options.A: To neutralize chemical toxins released by resident skin flora
options.B: To eliminate all pathogenic microorganisms from the sterile field
options.C: To reduce the total number of bacteria on non-porous furniture
options.D: To remove visible dirt and oil from the patient's outer skin

explanation: Aseptic technique aims to protect susceptible body sites by ensuring zero pathogens are introduced during invasive tasks. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which dimension of health involves the ability to handle daily stress and express feelings properly?

options.A: Spiritual dimension
options.B: Emotional dimension
options.C: Intellectual dimension
options.D: Environmental dimension

explanation: The emotional dimension focuses on mental resilience, coping mechanisms, and emotional expression. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the job of the sticky adhesive pads that come with an AED?

options.A: Secure the patient firmly to the flat floor surface
options.B: Deliver a continuous supply of medical oxygen to the lungs
options.C: Transmit electrical current from the machine to the patient's heart
options.D: Measure the exact body temperature of the victim

explanation: The pads act as the bridge. They stick to the skin to read the heart rhythm and deliver the life-saving shock safely. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why does a lack of financial transparency harm grassroots health committees?

options.A: It destroys community trust and discourages local donations and participation
options.B: It causes international pharmaceutical companies to raise drug prices
options.C: It forces health workers to close all clinics permanently
options.D: It automatically stops the federal government from paying nurse salaries

explanation: When villagers suspect mismanagement of local health funds, they lose faith in the committee and refuse to support health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why must used needles and razor blades go straight into a puncture-proof sharps box?

options.A: To comply with waste disposal rules without needing to wash them first
options.B: To ensure that they can be easily sharpened and reused for the next patient
options.C: To keep the delivery tray looking neat and tidy during the procedure
options.D: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and bloodborne pathogen transmission

explanation: Sharps safety keeps everyone safe! Dropping them right in the box protects you, your colleagues, and waste handlers from nasty infections like HIV or hepatitis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h7)

question: How is an epidemic different from an endemic disease?

options.A: An endemic illness only appears once every ten years in a community.
options.B: An epidemic represents a sudden spike in cases above the normal expected baseline.
options.C: An endemic condition spreads much faster than any known epidemic.
options.D: An epidemic only affects people living in cold weather climates.

explanation: Great thinking! While an endemic disease is steady and expected, an epidemic breaks that baseline with an unusual, sudden surge of new cases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T76#GNS214_U1_T76_h1)

question: Why is nursing care for a baby with tetanus focused on keeping the room dark and quiet?

options.A: To help the infant sleep and recover eyesight
options.B: To stop the bacterial growth in the dark room
options.C: To prevent sensory stimuli from triggering painful spasms
options.D: To prevent the development of infant jaundice

explanation: Spot on! Bright lights and loud noises can easily set off severe, exhausting muscle spasms, so a calm environment is key to healing. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h6)

question: How does a large local reaction differ from a normal insect sting reaction?

options.A: It indicates that bacteria have entered the wound and caused pus
options.B: It involves swelling greater than ten centimeters that peaks after a couple of days
options.C: It always causes immediate closing of the airway and low blood pressure
options.D: It means the patient is having a systemic IgE-mediated allergic response

explanation: Correct! A large local reaction is just a bigger, exaggerated inflammatory response at the site—it looks scary and spreads past 10cm, but it is not a true whole-body allergy. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h2)

question: What simple tool do nurses use to plot a child's weight against their age during clinic visits?

options.A: Patient temperature log
options.B: Road to Health chart
options.C: Blood pressure record sheet
options.D: Surgical safety checklist

explanation: You nailed it! The Road to Health chart is a handy visual tool we use everywhere to track how well a child is growing over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h3)

question: If your ward has a severe shortage of nursing assistants, what is a likely result for you as the registered nurse team leader?

options.A: Being exempted from all clinical ward duties
options.B: Having more time to focus purely on complex patient management
options.C: Spending extra time performing basic domestic or clerical chores
options.D: Automatic promotion to hospital director

explanation: That's correct! When support staff are missing, professional nurses often have to step in to cover basic tasks, which cuts into time for leadership and assessments. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h7)

question: What do we mean by the 'second victim' in healthcare?

options.A: The family members who witness a patient's decline
options.B: The secondary patient sharing a room with the affected individual
options.C: The healthcare professionals who experience emotional trauma after an error
options.D: The hospital institution that faces lawsuits and financial fines

explanation: The 'second victim' is the nurse or doctor who suffers deep emotional pain and stress after being involved in an unexpected patient incident. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which screening test uses a low-dose X-ray to spot tiny lumps and microcalcifications before anyone can even feel them?

options.A: Clinical inspection
options.B: Breast self-examination
